gex_data.gamma_regime: Negative modeled dealer gamma. Signed net GEX estimates range from -$40.47B to -$27.63B per 1% SPX move across GEX Metrix, SquawkFlow, Sikuli Research and ZeroGEX, with different expiration coverage and model assumptions. October 14 closing SPX 7718.94 is below all reported gamma-flip levels.

dealer_positioning.gamma_regime: Net short dealer gamma is indicated by multiple October 14 close and October 15 delayed SPX models. Reported zero-gamma flips range from 7740 (SquawkFlow) to 7787 (GEX Metrix); 7757 is Sikuli Research's October 14 close estimate. Dealer inventory signs are inferred from option open interest, not directly observed.
dealer_positioning.volatility_behavior: In a negative-gamma regime, modeled dealer hedging can reinforce price moves and increase intraday volatility. October 14 SquawkFlow's near-spot heatmap shows the largest negative displayed strike exposure at 7700 (about -$5.9B per 1% move) and strongest positive displayed near-spot strike at 7780 (about +$0.76B); these are not full-chain maxima.
dealer_positioning.expected_behavior: Watch 7700 as the nearest major negative-gamma concentration and put wall in near-term models, 7740-7787 as the model-dependent gamma-flip zone, and 7785 as SquawkFlow's volatility trigger. Broader-chain SquawkFlow call wall is 7900 and put wall 7500; ZeroGEX instead reports call wall 7800 and put wall 7700. S&P 500 futures are down about 0.32% before the open after October 14's inflation-driven selloff; PPI and retail-sales releases add event risk.

options_flow.skew: October 14 SPX 25-delta implied-volatility skew was +0.050 under Options Analysis Suite's call-minus-put convention (calls richer than puts). Vendor sign conventions differ; this is not directly comparable to put-minus-call risk reversals.
options_flow.zero_dte_dominance: October 15 realized 0DTE volume share is not available before the open. SquawkFlow's October 14 close heatmap assigns about -$14.5B of displayed near-spot gamma to the October 15 expiration, versus -$32.8B across the displayed 10-expiration grid; this is gamma concentration, not a trading-volume share.

volatility_surface.term_structure: October 14 SPX ATM IV was 13.2% with IV rank 20.0% and IV percentile 42.5%. The 30-35 DTE ATM IV range was approximately 12.9%-13.2%; 1DTE and 2DTE were 15.0% and 14.6%, respectively, indicating elevated front-end event premium and a non-monotonic curve. Options Analysis Suite reported a -0.003 fitted term-structure slope. Premarket VIX 17.48 is an indicative early quote, not synchronized with the 08:26 ET futures reading.
